subject: Propulsion AI: Draft MAP + Evaluation Playbook for trial
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Romero <alex@propulsion.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 4 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Propulsion AI: Draft MAP + Evaluation Playbook for trial

Alex —

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. Per our call I put together an initial mutual action plan (MAP) and a short evaluation playbook that outlines the acceptance criteria we typically use for a 30–45 day proof-of-value. The goal here is to give your engineering and product teams a clear runbook so we can get to a reliable acceptance signal quickly.

What I attached/linked here:
- MAP_template_v1.gdoc (Google Doc): living MAP that we can co-edit — includes stakeholder lanes, milestone owners, and acceptance criteria.
- Propulsion_MAP_kickoff.pptx: 2-slide kickoff summary you can drop into an internal update.

High-level ask from us: please review the doc and share the list of Propulsion stakeholders who will own each lane (security, infra, product, biz ops). If you can confirm a target ‘acceptance by’ date (we suggested 2027-01-15 as a tentpole) we’ll draft a concrete week-by-week runbook and lock in a kickoff slot.

Quick notes in the doc:
- Technical readiness: sample dataset, SSO test user, network egress to our staging cluster.
- Success metrics: 1) latency under 350ms for core flows, 2) 80% of golden prompts meet quality bar on first pass, 3) no PII leakage during the trial.

Looping in Marissa (Customer Success) and Ben (Solutions) on this thread to help with sequencing and security checklist.

Next steps:
1) You confirm stakeholders + preferred kickoff window (we have Wed/Thu next week open).
2) We co-edit MAP and finalize SOW-lite + timeline.
3) Kickoff workshop (60–90m) and engineering readiness call.

Attachments referenced as stubs; full doc link below.

Google Doc (editable): https://docs.google.com/document/d/1XPropulsionMAPDraft
Slides (view): https://drive.google.com/file/d/Propulsion_MAP_kickoff_slide_stub

Thanks — excited to get rolling.

—
Naomi Feldman
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com

Date: Fri, 4 Dec 2026 11:00:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Propulsion AI: Draft MAP + Evaluation Playbook for trial

Thanks Naomi — appreciate the quick turnaround and the structure. I skimmed the doc and it looks good as a starting point. A couple of asks from our side: 

- Can you add a short section on data handling during the trial (especially around transient logs and model caching)? Our security team will want to see what’s captured.
- Product would like to push the acceptance date out two weeks to allow time for an internal integration sprint (so tentatively 2027-01-29). Is that workable?
- Can you include an explicit procurement / contracting lane? We need to loop in procurement early so the purchase order doesn’t slow things down.

Also copying our Head of Product, Samantha, who will coordinate the engineering stakeholders. We can do Tue or Thu next week for a 60m call.

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: RE: Propulsion AI: Draft MAP + Evaluation Playbook for trial

Nice start — I made a few suggested edits and redlines in a local doc (attached). Key proposed tweaks:

1) Procurement lane: add PO milestone + procurement owner (legal sig / billing) with estimated 10 business-day lead.
2) Security lane: include SOC 2 scoping doc and a short checklist for what evidence we’ll provide (audit logs, encryption-in-flight-at-rest notes).
3) Engineering milestones: split week 2 into “integration verification” (SSO + staging traffic) and “performance tuning” (batching / KV cache configuration).
4) Acceptance: break into soft acceptance (functional validation) vs. hard acceptance (SLA signoff + billing enablement).

Draft week-by-week suggestion (6 weeks total):
- Week 0: Kickoff workshop, stakeholder RACI, access provisioning.
- Week 1: Data prep + SSO smoke tests.
- Week 2: Integration verification & baseline performance tests.
- Week 3: Feature validation against golden prompts, fix iteration.
- Week 4: Scale testing & cost tuning.
- Week 5: Acceptance validation & exec review.

I attached MAP_propulsion_redlined.docx with inline comments. Marissa — can you flag any onboarding support tickets we should create in Customer Success so nothing slips?

Subject: Propulsion AI: Updated MAP & proposed 6-week timeline (links inside)

Alex / Samantha —

Thanks for the feedback — Ben and Marissa jumped on the redlines and I incorporated the procurement and security lanes. I also adjusted the suggested acceptance date to 2027-01-29 to match your integration window.

The updated, editable MAP is here (co-edit enabled):
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1XPropulsionMAPDraft/edit?usp=sharing

Updated kickoff slide (slide only):
https://drive.google.com/file/d/Propulsion_MAP_kickoff_slide_stub_v2

Proposed condensed 6-week timeline (final suggestion):
- Week 0 (kickoff): stakeholder RACI, shared calendar, access provisioning, QA dataset delivery.
- Week 1: SSO + infra connectivity checks, baseline perf.
- Week 2: Integration verification (webhooks/ingest), first-pass functional validation.
- Week 3: Model configuration and quality iteration (golden set).
- Week 4: Scale testing and cost/profile tuning.
- Week 5: Acceptance validation, executive demo, procurement/PO processed.

Action items for Propulsion: please confirm the primary owners for these lanes by EOD Thu (security, product eng, procurement, biz ops). If you can share a preferred kickoff slot, we’ll send a calendar invite and a short agenda (60m).

I also added a short section in the doc that lists what evidence we’ll provide for security/scoped audit items (sample logs, diagram, retention policy). If your security team needs more detail we can set a 30m sync with our security engineer.

Thanks — looking forward to the kickoff.

—
